summary: Andrew Stirling (1793–1830) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at East India Company College (1811–1812) and Fort William College (~1813–1814). He served in the Political Department of the East India Company (~1820–1830).

Andrew Watsky (born 1957) is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1987–1994), and he held a post at Vassar College (~1993–2006).
Andrew William Kennedy is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds under the doctoral supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott (attested 2006).

Indologist and linguist Andrey Klebanov earned his MA and Dr. Phil. at the University of Hamburg, supervised by Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include Kyoto University (2016–2021), University of Alberta (2021), and University of Vienna (2022–2026).

Andrey Terentyev (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1969–1975) and the Russian Academy of Sciences (PhD 1980–1983), and he held a post at the Museum of History of Religion (~1984–1992).

Andrey Zaliznyak (1935–2017) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University, the University of Paris, and the Sorbonne under scholars including Louis Renou. He held posts at Moscow State University (~1960–1982) and the Russian Academy of Sciences (1960).

Andrzej Gawroński (1885–1927) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Lviv and the University of Leipzig (PhD 1905–1908), and he held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917), University of Lviv (1917), and University of Warsaw (1920).

Andrzej Ługowski (1938–2006) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań and the University of Warsaw under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz, and he taught at the University of Warsaw (~1961–2006).

András Róna-Tas (born 1931) is a scholar in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and held posts at Eötvös Loránd University, University of Szeged (1968–2002), and University of Vienna.

André Bareau (1921–1993) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne, and EPHE under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at CNRS, EPHE (1956–1973), and Collège de France (1971–1991).

André Caquot (1923–2004) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and École Pratique des Hautes Études, and he held posts at the University of Strasbourg, EPHE, University of Paris, and Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture (born 1945) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1966–1970), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1972–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1972–1977), and held a post at Laval University (~1978–2011).

André Godard (1881–1965) was a history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts. He held posts with DAFA (1923), the Archaeological Service of Iran (~1928–1953), and the University of Tehran (~1934–1949).

André Martinet (1908–1999) was a linguist who studied at the University of Paris and Sorbonne under Joseph Vendryes and Antoine Meillet. He held posts at EPHE (1938–1946), Columbia University (1947–1955), University of Paris (~1955–1970), and Paris Descartes University (~1970–1977).

André Mazon (1881–1967) was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1900–1904) and Charles University (~1902–1903). He served as a professor at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.
André Oltramare (1822–1896) was a scholar who held a post at the University of Geneva as Professor of Latin from approximately 1856 to 1886.

André Padoux (1920–2017) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Louis Renou and Olivier Lacombe, among others, and held posts as director at Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959–1964) and Directeur de Recherche at CNRS (~1964–1985).

André Wedemeyer (1875–1958) was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies under August Conrady (~1900–1903) and later held a post at the University of Leipzig.

Andy Rotman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins. He holds posts at Smith College (attested 2013–2026) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Anett Krause specializes in Indology, computational studies, and history/archaeology, earning degrees from Halle-Wittenberg and Marburg (Dr. phil. 2016). She held research posts at Leipzig University Library, Marburg, Halle-Wittenberg, Mainz Academy, and Royal Library of Berlin.
